headline: Mistakes to Avoid in Your Full Kitchen Renovation
articleBody:
Embarking on a full kitchen renovation for your Dallas–Fort Worth home is an exciting venture, but there are common pitfalls homeowners can encounter. Avoiding these mistakes can save you time, money, and stress, ensuring a smoother journey to your dream kitchen.

1. Starting Demolition Before Finalizing Selections — How to avoid it: Ensure all cabinetry, appliances, countertops, and finishes are selected and ordered before any demolition begins. Lead times for custom items can be significant, and starting too early can leave you with an unusable kitchen while waiting for materials.

2. Underestimating Lead Times — How to avoid it: Work closely with your design-build partner to get realistic estimates for material delivery, especially for custom cabinetry or imported stone. Factor these into your project timeline to avoid unexpected delays.

3. Comparing Bids with Different Scopes — How to avoid it: Always ensure that renovation quotes from different contractors cover the exact same scope of work, including structural changes, permit coordination, and specific material allowances. AKN Design Group provides upfront, transparent estimates that detail everything included.

4. Overlooking Temporary Living Arrangements — How to avoid it: Plan for where and how you’ll cook, wash dishes, and store food for the duration of the renovation. Setting up a temporary kitchen area minimizes daily inconvenience.

5. Neglecting Dust Control and Home Protection — How to avoid it: Discuss with your contractor how they will manage dust and protect the rest of your home. Proper sealing of work areas and covering furniture is crucial for a cleaner renovation experience.

6. Not Documenting Changes in Writing — How to avoid it: Any changes to the original plan, scope, or materials should always be documented in a written change order, detailing costs and revised timelines. This ensures clarity and prevents misunderstandings.
